page: Amazon Web Services c5d.large is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8124M processor operating at 3.4 GHz. This configuration provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a 2.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. It includes 50 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. In stress-ng single-core CPU testing, the instance achieves an average rating with a score of 1484.88, and single-threaded gzip compression registers an average throughput of 23.82 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-intensive benchmarks show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is rated poor at 1953.77, and Geekbench multi-core scores are similarly low at 1339.0. Memory bandwidth tests, such as large-block read and write operations, fall into the bottom 10% tier, measuring 12.85 GB/sec and 11.51 GB/sec respectively.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c5d.large offers a dedicated CPU allocation and high-speed local NVMe storage within a low-resource footprint, making it a viable entry point for workloads requiring fast local scratch space without massive memory overhead. Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, the instance is suited for lightweight compute-heavy tasks, single-threaded batch processing, basic web serving, and development environments that benefit from low-latency local storage but do not demand high memory bandwidth or multi-threaded scaling.
